bug_semantics: An authenticated builder can supply an upload filename containing ../ path segments. Budibase's pinned sanitize-s3-objectkey path preserves dot segments, so the APPS-bucket object key retains them. During workspace export, retrieveDirectory splits that S3 key on '/' and joins the segments beneath a temporary directory; Node path resolution consumes the .. segments and the unchecked filesystem write escapes the export directory, writing attacker-controlled bytes anywhere writable by the Budibase process.
flaw_origin: The unsafe S3-key-to-filesystem-path primitive originated in 1f36eec89a7faa297b6a589536b0110c6327639c, which added listAllObjects and retrieveDirectory and wrote each object's Key through join(writePath, ...Key.split('/')) without containment. Its direct parent already had sanitizeKey, which preserved dot segments, but had no retrieveDirectory sink. Export reachability followed in 8d7f40e443a6ee81f6cdfdc8651f98b4b45d927b; the later AI-file upload source in 6cf35343b0e7d24706a9b28292d410d958d0b9df placed input.filename directly into an APPS key. TypeScript conversion, streaming, tracing, and concurrency commits only moved or refactored the already-vulnerable sink.
ai_marker: absent — the exact BIC commit object names author and committer mike12345567 <me@michaeldrury.co.uk>; its message is 'Some updates towards supporting attachments in app exports.' and contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI trailer/marker.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/Budibase/budibase/security/advisories/GHSA-pxwc-66g3-5f27 is the repository advisory referenced by assigned GHSA-ccjw-whgg-h4gh/CVE-2026-72850. It identifies packages/backend-core/src/objectStore/objectStore.ts sanitizeKey and retrieveDirectory, packages/server/src/sdk/workspace/backups/exports.ts, packages/server/src/sdk/workspace/ai/knowledgeBase/uploads.ts, packages/server/src/api/controllers/ai/files.ts, and the builder-gated POST /api/backups/export path; it states that sanitize-s3-objectkey@0.0.1 preserves .. and that path.join resolves poisoned keys outside the temporary directory.

At the advisory's cited vulnerable snapshot 3c8d1b4023e17b4a7a5e7ca2307ef9de371a3632, git grep finds packages/backend-core/src/objectStore/objectStore.ts:95 returning sanitize(...).replace(/\\/g, '/'), line 593 splitting filename on '/', and line 601 calling fs.createWriteStream(join(writePath, ...possiblePath)). The same tree takes upload.originalFilename at packages/server/src/api/controllers/ai/files.ts:189, builds the APPS key in packages/server/src/sdk/workspace/ai/knowledgeBase/uploads.ts:42-48/60, and calls retrieveDirectory during export at packages/server/src/sdk/workspace/backups/exports.ts:129. The route is builder-gated at packages/server/src/api/routes/backup.ts:5-9.

git log -L and git -S history trace the vulnerable sink through later refactors to https://github.com/Budibase/budibase/commit/1f36eec89a7faa297b6a589536b0110c6327639c. That commit newly adds packages/backend-core/src/objectStore/index.ts:264-281; lines 274-279 split the S3 Key, create directories with join(writePath, ...dirs), and write with fs.writeFileSync(join(writePath, ...possiblePath), data). Commit 3d3a14e7ebdac0ff69205080592c67dfcfc8c703 merely changed the same loop to bounded concurrency, and d3c4c99e167354c682b2585834ca656c6c910772 merely moved it during TypeScript conversion, so neither is the smallest BIC.

Direct-parent proof: git cat-file identifies 9efb8f98bc4a105e00680eae97ed6d0916ada783 as the sole parent of 1f36eec89a7faa297b6a589536b0110c6327639c. git grep for retrieveDirectory and possiblePath in that parent's packages/backend-core/src/objectStore/index.ts returns no matches, while the BIC tree has retrieveDirectory at line 264, possiblePath at lines 274-276, and the unchecked write at line 279. The BIC diff creates those lines rather than moving them.

The direct fix is https://github.com/Budibase/budibase/commit/80d1ad98e801cfb1808489d2b5eb8a64da9d0544 ('Contain object store retrieval paths'). In packages/backend-core/src/objectStore/objectStore.ts it makes sanitizeKey reject '.' and '..' segments and replaces the unchecked write with getSafeRetrieveDirectoryPath, which resolve()s the target and accepts it only when it equals the export root or starts with root + path.sep; the commit also adds traversal regression coverage. This closes both poisoned-key creation and export-time containment failure.

Release-boundary verification from repository tags is stronger and more precise than the advisory's declared before-3.40.0/3.40.0 boundary: tag 3.39.23 resolves to 5a859aef87fa49c30195ab82af2750ea6bf94103, contains the BIC, does not contain 80d1ad98e801cfb1808489d2b5eb8a64da9d0544, and still has the unchecked createWriteStream at objectStore.ts:601. Tag 3.39.24 resolves to 3c86b6ab5d3f36c2bb668d6b44a17cfc32082785, is the first 3.39.x tag containing the fix, and has both the traversal rejection and getSafeRetrieveDirectoryPath. Tag 3.40.0 resolves to 661fe55d609404d073eea86702e0bde7942c3f10 and also contains the fix. Thus 3.39.23 is the last vulnerable 3.39 tag, 3.39.24 is the first fixed repository tag, and the declared patched boundary 3.40.0 is fixed but not the earliest fixed tag.

BIC-only AI attribution: numactl-prefixed git cat-file -p 1f36eec89a7faa297b6a589536b0110c6327639c shows one parent, human author/committer mike12345567 <me@michaeldrury.co.uk>, and only the plain commit subject with no trailers. No PR body, branch name, later refactor, or fix-commit signal was used for attribution.
reasoning: The pre-BIC tree could store S3 keys whose sanitizer preserved dot segments, but it did not contain the filesystem materialization loop. The BIC first created that unsafe trust-boundary crossing by interpreting every listed S3 Key as local path components and writing without proving the resolved target stayed under writePath; its direct parent lacks the function and lines. The export caller activated the sink two days later, and subsequent user-controlled filename upload paths made a poisoned workspace key directly reachable to authenticated builders. Refactors preserved the same unchecked join until 80d1ad98e801cfb1808489d2b5eb8a64da9d0544 added both segment rejection and defense-in-depth containment. Tagged trees prove the vulnerable/fixed transition and show 3.40.0 contains the fix, with the fix already present in 3.39.24. Because the smallest BIC's exact commit object is human-authored/committed and has no AI marker, the causal verdict is NOT_AI.
